page.title: AI Consultant vs Automation Agency: How to Choose
page.description: Compare scope, pricing, ownership and timelines so you pick the right partner for AI workflows or automation builds.
page.h1: How do you decide on AI consultant vs automation agency consultant?
page.definition: An AI consultant is a specialist who assesses opportunities, selects tools and delivers a roadmap. An automation agency is a build partner that ships working integrations, documents them and often runs a support retainer.
page.quick_answer: Choose an AI consultant when you need strategy, use-case prioritisation and tool selection before any build. Choose an automation agency when the use cases are clear and you need production-ready workflows, integrations and ongoing maintenance.

sections.h2: What does each partner actually deliver?

blocks.p: Consultant output: an assessment, a prioritised use-case list, a tool choice and a roadmap. Agency output: working automations, integrations and documentation, often with a support retainer.

ul: Consultant: current-state audit, opportunity scoring, vendor shortlist, implementation plan
Agency: mapped processes, built connectors, error handling, monitoring dashboards, handoff docs
Consultant typically stops at sign-off; agency stays live through a retainer

blocks.p: Pricing models: day rate or fixed project for consultants; fixed build fee plus a monthly retainer for agencies.

sections.h2: Who owns the outcome after delivery?

blocks.p: Ownership sits with the buyer in both cases, but the handoff point differs. A consultant hands over a plan and expects your team or another vendor to execute. An agency hands over running workflows and usually stays on for fixes, version updates and scope changes.

ul: Consultant: knowledge transfer workshop, runbook, tool admin training
Agency: live environment access, shared credentials, SLA for break-fix
Clarify who updates prompts, API keys and logic when vendors change

sections.h2: What timeline should you expect from kickoff to value?

blocks.p: A consultant engagement often runs four to six weeks for assessment and roadmap. An agency build for a first workflow takes two to four weeks, then the retainer begins. Complex multi-system automations extend to eight to twelve weeks.

ol: Week one to two: discovery, access provisioning, process mapping
Week three to four: consultant delivers roadmap or agency ships MVP
Week five onward: consultant exits or agency enters retainer cycle

sections.h2: When do you need both instead of one?

blocks.p: You need both when the problem space is fuzzy but the ambition is large. The consultant frames the opportunity, selects the stack and writes the brief; the agency builds to that brief and runs the ongoing ops. This split avoids paying agency rates for strategy and consultant rates for maintenance.

ul: Run a paid discovery with a consultant first
Convert the roadmap into fixed-scope agency statements of work
Keep the consultant for quarterly roadmap reviews only

faq.q: Can an AI consultant also build the automations?
faq.a: Some consultants offer build sprints, but they usually lack the engineering capacity for production-grade integrations, monitoring and long-term support that an agency provides.

faq.q: Does an automation agency help choose AI tools?
faq.a: Agencies advise on tooling within the build scope, but they rarely run a vendor-agnostic assessment across your whole stack. Pair a short consultant review with the agency build for unbiased selection.

faq.q: What internal resources must I provide for each model?
faq.a: For a consultant: stakeholder time, data access, process owners. For an agency: API credentials, sandbox environments, a product owner for acceptance testing and a point of contact for the retainer.

faq.q: How do I measure ROI differently for each?
faq.a: Consultant ROI is measured by quality of roadmap, use-case prioritisation and avoided wrong-tool spend. Agency ROI is measured by workflow uptime, hours saved per month, error rate reduction and retainer cost versus headcount.

faq.q: What contract clauses protect me if the partnership stalls?
faq.a: Include phase gates with acceptance criteria, IP assignment for all code and prompts, data-return provisions, and a thirty-day termination for convenience on retainers. Define 'done' for each workflow before signing.
